hints.title: Run Length Encoding Recurrence
hints.text: The count and say sequence is generated by grouping identical consecutive characters in the previous term into count followed by character value.

hints.title: Pointer Run Boundary Scanning
hints.text: Scan the string term using two indices. While the current character matches the run start character, advance the index to compute frequency.

hints.title: Iterative Sequence Expansion
hints.text: Start with initial string 1. Repeat the run length compression step n minus one times, building the next term from count and digit concatenations.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countAndSay(self, n: int) -> str:
        cur = "1"
        for _ in range(n - 1):
            nxt = []
            i = 0
            while i < len(cur):
                count = 1
                while i + 1 < len(cur) and cur[i] == cur[i + 1]:
                    i += 1
                    count += 1
                nxt.append(str(count) + cur[i])
                i += 1
            cur = "".join(nxt)
        return cur
```

variables: M: total characters across sequence iterations
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M) time and O(M) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: String concatenation in an unbuffered loop incurs quadratic string copies per step.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: List-based character aggregation avoids intermediate string copies, achieving linear time in the output length.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should implement clear two-pointer run-length encoding without off-by-one errors on string boundaries.
